'''Thomas Henry Brylawski''' (June 17, 1944 – July 18, 2007) was an American mathematician and professor at the [[University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill]].  He worked primarily in [[matroid theory]].

==Education and career==
Brylawski was born in 1944, and grew up in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name="obitpaper">{{cite journal|last1=Gordon|first1=Gary|last2=McNulty|first2=Jennifer|author2-link=Jenny McNulty|title=Thomas H. Brylawski (1944–2007)|journal=European Journal of Combinatorics|volume=32|issue=6|year=2011|pages=712–721|issn=0195-6698|doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2011.02.009|mr=2821546|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="wapo">{{cite web|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/08/09/AR2007080902169_pf.html|title=Obituaries for August 10, 2007|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=November 9, 2019}}</ref> He attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for his undergraduate degree, finishing with a Bachelor of Science in 1966. He then went on to [[Dartmouth College]] for his graduate work. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] under the direction of [[Gian-Carlo Rota]] and Robert Norman in 1970.<ref name=mathgen>{{MathGenealogy|id=17985|name=Thomas Henry Brylawski}}</ref>  After his PhD, he moved to the [[University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill]], where he spent the rest of his career.<ref name="memorialpage">{{cite web|url=https://math.unc.edu/files/2015/07/Memorial-page-for-Professor-Thomas-Brylawski.pdf|title=Memorial page for Professor Thomas H. Brylawski|publisher=University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill Department of Mathematics}}</ref><ref name="obitpaper" />

Brylawski was an editor for the ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]'' from 1977 until 1989.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/journalsframework/proc/editorial_history_proc|title=Past Editorial Board Members|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|access-date=November 9, 2019}}</ref>  Brylawski wrote 40 mathematical publications,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=42695 |title=Thomas H. Brylawski author profile|website=[[MathSciNet]]|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and advised 6 PhD students.<ref name=mathgen />

He died in 2007 of [[esophageal cancer]] at the Duke Hospice inpatient facility in [[Hillsborough, North Carolina]].<ref name="wapo"/>

==Work==
Brylawski's early work used ideas and tools from [[category theory]] to understand the [[Tutte polynomial]] of a matroid. Indeed, this idea already appeared in his thesis, which made constructions in matroid theory similar to the [[Grothendieck group]].<ref>{{cite thesis|title=The Tutte-Grothendieck Ring|last=Brylawski|first=Thomas Henry|year=1970|publisher=Dartmouth College|type=PhD}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brylawski|first1=T. H.|title=The Tutte-Grothendieck Ring|journal=[[Algebra Universalis]]|volume=2|issue=1|year=1972|pages=375–388|issn=0002-5240|doi=10.1007/BF02945050|mr=0330004|s2cid=121150927}}</ref>  He developed similar ideas in two papers in the ''[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]''.<ref name="obitpaper" /><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brylawski|first1=Thomas|title=A Combinatorial Model for Series-Parallel Networks|journal=[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=154|year=1971|pages=1|issn=0002-9947|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1971-0288039-7|mr=0288039|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brylawski|first1=Thomas H.|title=A Decomposition for Combinatorial Geometries|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|volume=171|year=1972|pages=235–282|issn=0002-9947|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1972-0309764-6|mr=0309764|doi-access=free}}</ref> Another influential early paper of Brylawski's, published in the same journal, described the influence of a [[Modular lattice#Modular pairs and related notions|modular]] element in the lattice of [[flat (matroids)|flats]] on the [[Matroid#Characteristic polynomial|characteristic polynomial]] of a matroid.<ref name="obitpaper" /><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Brylawski|first1=Tom|title=Modular Constructions for Combinatorial Geometries|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|volume=203|year=1975|pages=1–44|issn=0002-9947|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1975-0357163-6|mr=0357163|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Brylawski also contributed expository chapters to several matroid theory books that appeared in the ''Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications'' series published by [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref name=obitpaper /> The Tutte polynomial chapter (written jointly with [[James Oxley]]) has around 500 citations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?cites=1480927036572787410|title=The Tutte Polynomials and its Applications (citations)|website=Google Scholar|access-date=March 15, 2021}}</ref>

In addition to his work in matroid theory, Brylawski also had an interest in mathematics in art, particularly in the role of symmetry in art.<ref name=obitpaper /> He gave lectures on mathematics in art on two occasions at the [[National Gallery of Art]] in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nga.gov/content/dam/ngaweb/research/gallery-archives/calendar-of-events/1960-1979/9A17_55524_197302.pdf|title=Calendar of Events for February 1973|publisher=[[National Gallery of Art]]|access-date=November 9, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nga.gov/content/dam/ngaweb/research/gallery-archives/calendar-of-events/1980-1999/9A17_55539_198804.pdf|title=Calendar of Events for April 1988|publisher=National Gallery of Art|access-date=November 9, 2019}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
A memorial conference was held in honor of Brylawski in October 2008 at the [[University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill]],<ref name="obitpaper" /> and a special issue of the ''[[European Journal of Combinatorics]]'' in 2011 was dedicated as a tribute to the work of Brylawski.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gordon|first1=Gary|last2=Oxley|first2=James|author2-link=James Oxley|title=Preface|journal=European Journal of Combinatorics|volume=32|issue=6|year=2011|pages=709–711|issn=0195-6698|doi=10.1016/j.ejc.2011.02.006|mr=2821545|doi-access=}}</ref>
